__doc: rate_well control in the sequential-implicit scheme (2026-08-15): robust base (growth loop + growth_driven_switch + contact hysteresis + width relaxation + onset hold) + control.type=rate_well + well_source_all_perfs + ITERATIVE coupled solver (bicgstab, mech-last, umfpack flow block). Physically the preferred control: the fracture pressure is solved for under the well's rate constraint, so it lands on the near-closure, leak-off-equilibrium state (closure+8 bar, ~500 m2 on model2) by itself, floor-INSENSITIVE (0.3 mm == 1 mm), and the BHP has Reveal's decaying shape after opening. The old NaN was the establishment death spiral (no growth loop) — NOT the linear solver; the direct solver is no longer needed (iterative 4.6x faster). KNOWN PROBLEMS: (1) the well row is a duplicated static single-well single-phase model (matrix WI/lambda/p_res frozen from the last flow solve, lambda=1) — not in sync with BlackoilWellModel BHP/THP/groups, one fracture per well; (2) the fracture is fed only where it exists: on multi-perforation wells the perforations outside the fracture stay matrix perfs and take their share (model2 4-perf: 30-40 %), which also holds the BHP 40-60 bar above Reveal until the fracture is tall enough; (3) opening looks late (well DOF ~650 bar) because the caked matrix perfs carry the rate until the fracture is big — physics, not a bug; (4) one day of testing vs months for perf_pressure. Requires WSEED WIDTH >= 3e-4 in the deck for a sane flow floor. Short caked model2: 109 s (2026-08-24, after the iterative-solver fix: lu_pivoting + scaling=blockmax + failure_policy=ladder - the coupled system is so ill-scaled during establishment that bicgstab/gmres overflow to defect=nan; the ladder rung 3 (drop-C block-triangular with exact flow+pivoted-LU mech solves) rescues those iterations; direct solver 458 s gives the same answer).
